name: The four deviations from emptiness (shor sa bzhi)
description: Deviating from the essence of emptiness (not recognizing it), into 'sealing' (labelling things empty), into the antidote (using emptiness as a remedy), and into the path (treating emptiness as something to reach later).

name: The three strayings (gol sa gsum)
description: Attachment to the meditative experiences of bliss, clarity and non-thought, which lead to rebirth in the desire, form and formless realms rather than to liberation.

equivalents.note: relishing meditative states is the common fault; the Kagyu maps each state to a realm

name: Clinging to meditative experiences and visions
description: Taking experiences, visions or miracles (in dream or waking) as real or as signs of attainment; held as real they are obstacles, known as illusion they become path.

equivalents.note: attachment to powers is one form of it

name: Dullness and agitation (bying rgod)
description: The two faults of śamatha: sinking/dullness and excitement/scattering; corrected by adjusting tightness and looseness.

name: Distraction (g.yeng ba)
description: Losing the recognition by following thoughts; non-distraction is 'the main body of meditation'.

name: Hope and fear (re dogs)
description: Hoping for results and fearing failure in practice; 'without hope and fear the fruit is manifest'.

name: Dualistic grasping (gzung 'dzin)
description: Grasping at apprehended object and apprehending subject, the root of attachment and aversion; when it collapses the illusory body is realized (Karṇatantravajrapada).

name: The two obscurations (sgrib gnyis)
description: The obscuration of afflictions and the obscuration of the knowable, the 'adventitious stains' that cover mind's luminous nature; self-purified in Mahāmudrā (Karṇatantravajrapada).

equivalents.note: the sūtra three obstructions include the two plus karma

name: Wind disorder from improper practice (rlung nad)
description: Forcing the breath and wind practices without the proper application, or without the guru's instruction, is taught to turn qualities into faults and to cause wind disorders.

equivalents.note: the haṭha warning that faulty breath control causes illness

name: The three kinds of laziness
description: Idleness, discouragement (self-deprecation) and attachment to unworthy activities, overcome by diligence (Jewel Ornament ch.15).
members: bya ba ngan zhen gyi le lo

name: The eight worldly conditions
description: Kagyu contribution: gain and loss, pleasure and pain, praise and blame, fame and disgrace — the 'eight worldly dharmas' Milarepa urges renouncing; self-liberated through the illusory body.

name: The three roots of bad (greed, hatred, delusion)
description: Kagyu contribution: in clear-light practice one looks without grasping at the three poisons; they are 'purified as body, speech and mind' (Tilopa).

name: The four Māras
description: Kagyu contribution: the demons Milarepa met at Red Rock Jewel Valley vanished when recognized as his own mind's projections.

name: Breaking the samaya pledges
description: Kagyu contribution: giving the sealed instructions to unfit vessels, or heedless, craving practice of the method path, breaks the pledge and leads to hell or lower realms.

name: The ten unwholesome courses of action
description: Kagyu contribution: the ten non-virtues and their results (Jewel Ornament ch.6).
